ordered_diagnoses: Intrauterine growth restriction with cerebral impairment

facts.raw_span: born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound had shown microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI of the head revealed microcephaly, marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions were seen
very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
No chorioretinal dysplasia was noted

concepts.why: The patient was born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation and weighed 2152 g, indicating growth restriction, and her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks, which may have contributed to the growth restriction.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed microcephaly, which is a condition where the head is significantly smaller than expected.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed ventricular enlargement, which is a characteristic of hydrocephalus.
The patient had very weak light reflexes bilaterally and mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign, which are indicative of optic nerve hypoplasia.
The patient had severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, which is consistent with periventricular leukomalacia.

concepts.preferred_label: Intrauterine growth restriction with cerebral impairment
concepts.why: The patient had intrauterine growth restriction, microcephaly, and ventricular enlargement, which are indicative of cerebral impairment due to intrauterine growth restriction.
It explains the marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure and the preservation of certain brain structures.
It explains the mild optic nerve pallor and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign.

rationales.F01: Preterm birth is associated with fetal growth restriction and intrauterine growth restriction with cerebral impairment.
rationales.F04: The death of a monochorionic diamniotic twin in utero may be related to fetal growth restriction and periventricular leukomalacia.
rationales.F05: Fetal ultrasound findings of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are strongly associated with microcephaly and congenital hydrocephalus.
rationales.F06: Postnatal MRI findings of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are strongly associated with microcephaly and congenital hydrocephalus.
rationales.F07: Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes is associated with microcephaly and periventricular leukomalacia.
rationales.F08: The preservation of certain brain structures may rule out some conditions, such as periventricular leukomalacia and congenital hydrocephalus.
rationales.F09: The absence of intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions may rule out some conditions, such as congenital hydrocephalus and periventricular leukomalacia.
rationales.F10: Weak light reflexes may be associated with optic nerve hypoplasia and optic atrophy.
rationales.F11: Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign is strongly associated with optic nerve hypoplasia and optic atrophy.

frontier_selector.rationale: Microcephaly is supported by both fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI findings, and is a direct explanation for the observed brain abnormalities, while optic nerve hypoplasia is also a strong candidate due to the observed weak light reflexes and optic nerve pallor.
